correctness.rationale: The universal estimate follows from the canonical boundary Fourier decomposition. For bounded harmonic \(f=h+\overline g\) with \(g(0)=0\), the boundary data \(F\in L^\infty(\mathbb T)\) satisfy \(P_+F=h^*\) and \(P_+\overline F-\overline{h(0)}=g^*\). The classical endpoint Riesz projection \(P_+:L^\infty\to\mathrm{BMO}\), followed by the analytic BMO identification and derivative-Carleson characterization, gives the stated uniform BMOA bound. Kalaj's Theorem 1 was read in the complete primary PDF: for every \(0<k<1\) it gives a bounded globally one-to-one harmonic map with \(|g'|\le k|h'|\) and unbounded \(h\), and explicitly identifies maximal dilatation \(K=(1+k)/(1-k)\). Choosing \(k=(K-1)/(K+1)\) gives every prescribed \(K>1\). If \(g\) were bounded then \(h=f-\overline g\) would be bounded, so both canonical components are unbounded while the first part puts both in BMOA.
